extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and researchers applying to or organizing programs at the Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach (workshops, miniworkshops, SVP, RiP, Leibniz Fellows, graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and program criteria for organizing, applying to, and participating in Oberwolfach scientific activities (workshops, miniworkshops, seminars, Research in Pairs, Simons Visiting Professors, Leibniz Fellows, graduate student support, and related awards/publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of the scientific program
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific program is decided by the Director in cooperation with the Scientific Committee of the Gesellschaft für Mathematische Forschung; the Committee examines all scientific events prior to approval and the program is fixed in a competitive procedure according to strictly scientific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scientific Committee is based on the honorary work of about 20–25 top-class mathematicians who cover the entire breadth of mathematics. The institute receives substantially more proposals than can be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop program format and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Main program consists of about 40 one-week workshops per year with about 50 participants (alternatively two half-size workshops of ~25 participants). Workshops are organized by internationally leading experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are invited personally by the Director on recommendation of the organizers. Workshops are research-oriented and intended to provide a stimulating atmosphere where many significant research projects originate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant invitation process for workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are invited on recommendation of the organizers and personally invited by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers (international leading experts) recommend participants; the Director issues invitations based on those recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Visiting Professors (SVP) eligibility and support
rubrics_metrics.description: SVP supports up to 40 distinguished scientists from outside Europe who wish to combine an Oberwolfach workshop invitation with a research visit to a European university of up to two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program provides support of 135 Euro per day of the university visit. Participating universities must provide accommodation for the visit duration and match the support regarding travel expenses within Europe between Oberwolfach and the university. SVP awards are decided by the Director on suggestion of the workshop organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mini-Workshop program criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve one-week Mini-Workshops per year, each with about 15 participants, aimed particularly at junior researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics are fixed only half a year before the event, allowing quick reaction to current developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Arbeitsgemeinschaft (study group) format
rubrics_metrics.description: Study groups meet twice yearly for one week; participants learn a new, current field by giving their own lectures under guidance of internationally recognized specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized (in the described text) by Prof. Christopher Deninger and Prof. Gerd Faltings; targeted at both junior and established researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Seminars target and format
rubrics_metrics.description: One-week seminars held six times per year, organized by leading experts, aimed at Ph.D. students and postdocs worldwide, introducing 25 participants to a particularly current research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seminars are designed to introduce participants to 'hot' developments; supported (in the period noted) by the Carl Friedrich von Siemens Foundation (2008–2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research in Pairs (RiP) program criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Small groups of 2–4 researchers from different institutions work together at MFO on a pre-defined project for between 2 weeks and 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program is aimed at focused collaborative projects and provides dedicated residency periods to facilitate concentrated joint research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Leibniz Fellows (postdoc) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral program supporting particularly qualified junior researchers for 2 to 6 months to carry out research projects at Oberwolfach, individually or in small groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical is the integration of Leibniz Fellows into an active research group with an established senior researcher at a university or research institute. The program cooperates with the European Post-Doctoral Institute (EPDI) network of well-known mathematical institutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Leibniz Graduate Students support rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Support (since 2009) for an average of five doctoral students per workshop (additional five places per workshop reserved for Leibniz Graduate Students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible are excellent doctoral students or recent Ph.D.s up to two years after the Ph.D.; support includes travel reimbursement. The five additional places per workshop may not be occupied by senior researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Reports (OWR) format and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: OWR is a book series (initiated 2004 with EMS) to make workshop results widely accessible; appears quarterly in an edition of 300 copies, comprising four issues and >3000 pages per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWR contain extended abstracts of all talks (one to three pages each) including references, documenting the high level of the events and many new discoveries introduced at the Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Prize and John Todd Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Oberwolfach Prize (about every three years) is awarded to European junior researchers for excellent achievements in rotating fields of mathematics; the John Todd Award (also ~every three years) is for junior researchers in numerical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary endowments: Oberwolfach Prize = 10,000 Euro; John Todd Award = 1,000 Euro.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scale and target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Different MFO programs have specified target audiences and typical sizes/durations (e.g., workshops ~50 participants/week, miniworkshops ~15 participants/week, seminars ~25 participants/week, RiP 2–4 researchers for 2 weeks–3 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are tailored to career stages (graduate students, postdocs, junior researchers, senior researchers) and to particular goals (research collaboration, intensive learning, outreach).
